headline: ChatGPT gets Scheduled tasks hub for future prompts
summary: OpenAI rolls out a new Scheduled page for managing future tasks
details: OpenAI has begun rolling out an update to ChatGPT that highlights its ability to handle scheduled tasks. The new Scheduled page allows users to see active tasks, including when they're set to run, and manage them.

The Scheduled page lets users pause, edit, and delete upcoming requests. OpenAI has also made ChatGPT's ability to handle scheduled prompts more robust, stating 'all tasks are faster and more reliable.'

Users can tell ChatGPT to complete tasks at a specific time or during a broader timeframe, such as morning, afternoon, or evening. The feature also allows for monitoring tasks, which proactively search the web or connected apps.

The new scheduled tasks experience is rolling out to Go, Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users on web and mobile. OpenAI is also sunsetting Pulse, its personalized daily summaries, with a 14-day grace period for Pro users.

headline_marked: Epic Games lets Fortnite skins into other games [[with Unreal Engine 6]]
headline: Epic Games lets Fortnite skins into other games with Unreal Engine 6
summary: Epic Games plans to allow developers to use Fortnite skins in other games built with Unreal Engine 6. The engine's next major version will enable cross-game character skins.
details: Epic Games is working on making its metaverse vision a reality with Unreal Engine 6. The company plans to let developers create games that can use player skins from Fortnite, as well as build their own skins compatible with the popular game.

The system, announced at Epic's State of Unreal keynote, aims to prove the concept of an interoperable metaverse. It will allow players to use their Fortnite purchases across multiple games, starting with a complex system that inherently provides player value.

Developers will need to implement support for the system in their games, which isn't a guarantee. Epic is targeting an early access release for Unreal Engine 6 by the end of 2027, with a full release coming 12-18 months later.
This move comes as Fortnite faces challenges, including a dropoff in engagement and recent layoffs of over 1,000 workers. Despite this, Fortnite still has 75 million monthly active users.
